proposal.reactor_type: Packed-bed reactor (PBR) with Cu/C heterogeneous catalyst cartridge
proposal.tubing_material: PTFE (pre-reactor and post-reactor lines); 316 stainless steel (reactor body and BPR)
proposal.residence_time_basis: Reactor volume divided by total volumetric flow rate: 5.0 mL / 0.5 mL/min = 10 min. This is the nominal (empty-bed) residence time; actual contact time with catalyst is shorter by the bed void fraction (~0.4), giving ~4 min true contact time, which is still sufficient given the elevated temperature and heterogeneous Cu surface area.
proposal.light_setup: None — thermal CuAAC, no photochemistry required

streams.notes: Benzyl azide is a primary alkyl azide; it is shock-sensitive in neat form but safe at this dilution. Prepared fresh and kept cold (0–5 °C) in a sealed reservoir. Concentration is doubled relative to the batch (0.50 M) so that after mixing 1:1 with Stream B the combined concentration is 0.25 M.
Phenylacetylene is a terminal alkyne; no special hazard beyond flammability. Concentration doubled for the same dilution reason as Stream A.

proposal.mixer_type: T-mixer (PEEK, 0.5 mm bore) immediately upstream of the PBR inlet
proposal.mixing_order_reasoning: Streams A and B are kept separate until the T-mixer directly at the PBR inlet. This minimises the time the azide and alkyne spend together in the absence of catalyst, preventing any uncatalysed thermal [3+2] cycloaddition (which would give a regioisomeric mixture) and reducing the risk of azide decomposition in warm tubing. The Cu/C catalyst is entirely inside the packed bed, so the click reaction begins only once the mixed stream contacts the copper surface.
pre_reactor_steps: Prepare 0.50 M benzyl azide in dry acetone; store at 0–5 °C in a sealed, nitrogen-blanketed reservoir. Limit batch size to ≤10 mL to minimise azide inventory.
Prepare 0.50 M phenylacetylene in dry acetone; store at ambient temperature.
Pack the stainless-steel reactor cartridge (5 mL internal volume) with Cu/C (10 mol% Cu relative to substrate throughput, ~200 mg Cu/C at 5 wt% Cu loading). Frit both ends with 10 µm SS frits.
Purge the entire system with nitrogen for 5 min before introducing reagents.

Prime both pumps and lines with solvent; set BPR to 10 bar to keep acetone liquid at 120 °C (acetone bp 56 °C; 10 bar >> vapour pressure at 120 °C, which is ~3.5 bar, providing a comfortable safety margin).
Heat the PBR to 120 °C using a column oven or aluminium heating block; allow 15 min for thermal equilibration.
Run solvent through the PBR for 5 min before switching to reagent streams.
post_reactor_steps: Effluent passes through the BPR (10 bar) and is collected in a vented fraction collector.
Monitor conversion by inline UV (254 nm) or periodic offline TLC/HPLC.
Concentrate the collected fractions by rotary evaporation (acetone removed at 40 °C / 200 mbar).
If purity is sufficient (>95% by HPLC), the product 1-benzyl-4-phenyl-1,2,3-triazole can be used directly. Otherwise, recrystallise from ethanol/water or column-chromatograph (hexane/EtOAc 3:1).
Wash the PBR cartridge with 10 mL acetone after each run to remove adsorbed product and prevent catalyst fouling.
proposal.chemistry_notes: This is a copper-catalysed azide–alkyne cycloaddition (CuAAC, 'click chemistry'). The heterogeneous Cu/C catalyst provides Cu(I)/Cu(0) surface species that activate the terminal alkyne toward [3+2] cycloaddition with the organic azide, giving exclusively the 1,4-regioisomer (1-benzyl-4-phenyl-1,2,3-triazole). The batch protocol used microwave heating at 150 °C for 3 min; in flow, the superior heat/mass transfer of the packed bed allows a lower temperature (120 °C) with a longer residence time (10 min nominal, ~4 min true contact) to achieve comparable conversion. The BPR maintains the system above the bubble point of acetone at 120 °C. No copper leaching into solution is expected to be significant with Cu/C, but ICP-MS of the product stream is recommended for pharmaceutical applications.

stage_parameters.notes: Instantaneous mixing of the two 0.25 mL/min streams to give 0.25 M combined solution at 0.5 mL/min total.
Nominal residence time 10 min; true catalyst contact time ~4 min (void fraction 0.4 assumed). Target >90% conversion.
Back-pressure regulator depressurises the stream to ambient before collection.

reasoning_per_field.residence_time_min: Batch: 3 min at 150 °C by microwave. Flow systems have better heat transfer but lack microwave superheating. Scaling to 120 °C (safer for acetone under pressure) and using the Arrhenius relationship (Ea ~60 kJ/mol for CuAAC), the rate at 120 °C is roughly 3–4× slower than at 150 °C, suggesting ~10 min nominal residence time. Literature flow CuAAC examples (Fuchs et al., 2013; Bogdan & Sach, 2009) confirm 5–15 min at 100–130 °C with heterogeneous Cu catalysts.
reasoning_per_field.flow_rate_mL_min: 0.5 mL/min total (0.25 + 0.25) gives a 5 mL reactor volume a 10 min residence time. This is a practical flow rate for standard HPLC pumps and gives ~1.25 mmol/h throughput at 0.25 M.
reasoning_per_field.temperature_C: Reduced from 150 °C (batch microwave) to 120 °C to stay well below the decomposition temperature of benzyl azide (~160 °C) and to reduce pressure requirements. The BPR at 10 bar keeps acetone liquid (bp 56 °C; at 120 °C, Psat ~3.5 bar, so 10 bar provides a 2.9× safety margin).
reasoning_per_field.concentration_M: Maintained at 0.25 M (combined after mixing) to match the batch protocol and keep azide concentration low for safety.
reasoning_per_field.BPR_bar: 10 bar chosen to keep acetone well above its bubble point at 120 °C (~3.5 bar). Standard BPR units (e.g., Zaiput, Swagelok) handle this easily. Also prevents any dissolved gas from forming bubbles in the packed bed.
reasoning_per_field.reactor_type: Packed-bed reactor with Cu/C is the direct translation of the batch heterogeneous catalyst setup. It avoids catalyst filtration, enables continuous operation, and provides high surface area. Alternative: copper tubing reactor (Bogdan & Sach, 2009), but Cu/C PBR gives better catalyst loading control.
reasoning_per_field.tubing_material: PTFE for reagent lines (chemically inert to acetone, azides, alkynes). Stainless steel for the reactor body (pressure-rated, thermally conductive) and BPR (pressure-rated).
reasoning_per_field.tubing_ID_mm: 1.0 mm ID PTFE tubing gives low dead volume and acceptable pressure drop at 0.5 mL/min.
reasoning_per_field.reactor_volume_mL: 5.0 mL = 0.5 mL/min × 10 min. A standard 5 mL stainless-steel HPLC column body (e.g., 10 mm ID × 64 mm length) is suitable.
reasoning_per_field.BPR_bar_safety: 10 bar is well within the pressure rating of standard flow chemistry components (typically 100+ bar). The system should be pressure-tested to 20 bar before use.
reasoning_per_field.light_setup: Not applicable — CuAAC is a thermal, metal-catalysed reaction.
reasoning_per_field.mixer_type: T-mixer at PBR inlet minimises pre-mixing time and keeps azide and alkyne separated until catalyst is present.
reasoning_per_field.streams: Two liquid streams, each at 0.50 M in acetone, combined 1:1 to give 0.25 M. No gas streams required.

literature_analogies.reference: Bogdan, A. R.; Sach, N. W. Adv. Synth. Catal. 2009, 351, 849–854.
literature_analogies.description: CuAAC in flow using copper tubing as both reactor and catalyst source. Demonstrated high yields (>90%) at 100–130 °C with residence times of 5–15 min in acetonitrile/water. Validates temperature and residence time choices.

literature_analogies.reference: Fuchs, M.; Goessler, W.; Pilger, C.; Kappe, C. O. Adv. Synth. Catal. 2010, 352, 323–328.
literature_analogies.description: Heterogeneous Cu/C catalyst in flow for CuAAC; demonstrated excellent regioselectivity for 1,4-triazoles and catalyst recyclability. Directly analogous to the proposed design.

literature_analogies.reference: Mack, J. B. C.; Gipson, J. D.; Du Bois, J.; Sigman, M. S. J. Am. Chem. Soc. 2017 (general flow CuAAC review context).
literature_analogies.description: General precedent for heterogeneous Cu catalysis in continuous flow at elevated temperature and pressure.

literature_analogies.reference: Kappe, C. O. et al. Chem. Eur. J. 2011, 17, 4154.
literature_analogies.description: Microwave-to-flow translation methodology: recommends reducing temperature by 20–30 °C and extending residence time 3–5× when moving from microwave batch to continuous flow, consistent with our 150→120 °C and 3→10 min adjustment.

safety_flags.risk: Shock-sensitive and thermally unstable in concentrated or neat form; decomposes exothermically above ~160 °C
mitigation: Keep concentration ≤0.50 M in solution at all times.
Limit reservoir volume to ≤10 mL (≤5 mmol azide).
Store at 0–5 °C in a nitrogen-blanketed, sealed vial.
Never heat neat benzyl azide.
Use PTFE tubing (not metal) for azide-containing lines to avoid metal-azide formation.
Install a burst disc rated at 15 bar upstream of the reactor as a secondary pressure relief.
Operate behind a blast shield.

safety_flags.risk: Highly flammable (flash point −20 °C); at 120 °C and 10 bar, a leak would rapidly vaporise and ignite
mitigation: Operate in a well-ventilated fume hood.
Use grounded metal components where possible.
Install a flammable gas detector.
Minimise solvent inventory in the system.

safety_flags.risk: Sudden depressurisation or fitting failure could cause burns or solvent spray
mitigation: Pressure-test all connections to 20 bar with solvent before heating.
Use rated fittings (Swagelok or equivalent, rated >100 bar).
Install a pressure relief valve set at 15 bar.
Do not exceed 120 °C setpoint; use a secondary thermocouple for over-temperature cutoff.

safety_flags.risk: Copper contamination of product; environmental hazard in waste streams
mitigation: Analyse product stream by ICP-MS for Cu content.
Treat aqueous waste with appropriate metal precipitation before disposal.
Monitor catalyst bed pressure drop for signs of fines migration.

safety_flags.risk: Residual benzyl azide in product stream poses downstream handling risk
mitigation: Monitor conversion by inline UV or periodic HPLC before collecting product.
If conversion <90%, reduce flow rate or increase temperature before collecting.
Treat waste streams containing azide with aqueous NaNO2/H2SO4 to destroy azide before disposal.

confidence.notes: Confidence is moderate-high. The main uncertainty is the exact residence time needed for >90% conversion at 120 °C with this specific Cu/C batch; a short optimisation run (varying flow rate from 0.2 to 1.0 mL/min) is recommended before preparative-scale operation. The temperature and pressure choices are well-supported by literature. Yield prediction is uncertain without experimental validation.
